newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates surge to 4.25/4.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates surge to 4.25/4.50 pct.

text.p: German call money rates surged above the four percent level on Monday as liquidity conditions tightened further while banks scrambled to meet month-end reserve requirements.

Traders said overnight funds traded between 4.25/4.50 percent this morning compared with rates of 3.00/3.05 percent on Friday and forecast that borrowings at the Lombard emergency rate would be quite high.
"Lombard borrowings could be around 10 billion marks," one dealer predicted.
But dealers said the jump in rates did not catch the market by surprise as liquidity conditions had already begun to tighten at the end of last week.
Usually rates return to normal during the first several days of the new month after banks have repayed Lombard borrowings.
Banks held 40.2 billion marks in reserve at the Bundesbank on Friday compared with 40.4 billion marks a day earlier.
Average holdings on Friday nudged slightly higher to 38.7 billion marks compared with 38.5 billion marks. Lombard borrowings were unchanged at 100 million marks on Friday.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was set at 4.50003 percent on Monday compared with 3.08050 percent on Friday.
